structure: M-outer; fused SBUF RMSNorm (square -> single full-1024 free-axis reduce -> rsqrt(scale=1/K) -> per-row [128,1] tensor_scalar); all-w-resident (64KB/part) + single x load; identity-transpose xn -> [k_in,m_in]; K-accumulate 8 tiles into [128,512] fp32 PSUM; stream 4 N-chunks
rsqrt_form: folded rsqrt(sumsq*1/K), single full-K reduce (numpy+Codex confirmed identical to baseline scale-before-reduce, ~1.3e-7)
notes: First correct kernel (phase 1). fp32, full 5-seed L2 PASS, 1.066x over baseline. PE-bound at fp32 floor (MFU~46%); RMSNorm cheap/overlapped (Vec 15% Scl 11%), fusion removed HBM round-trip. Phase-2 targets: transpose overhead (256 fp32 transpose matmuls), fp32 PE floor.

Same-session v1 control (phase-2 round 0) to anchor the noise band. 0.4715 ms vs historical 0.4716 -> drift <0.03%. PE_active_ms=0.97*0.4715=0.4574 (PE% is whole-percent-rounded, so treat as a coarse proxy). Fair comparison point for all phase-2 candidates (AC-4/AC-6).

structure: Post-scale eviction fold: transpose RAW x (still on PE via identity nc_matmul), matmul into fp32 PSUM, apply per-row [128,1] inv_rms at PSUM->SBUF eviction via tensor_scalar reading the PSUM accumulator DIRECTLY (no nl.copy). Removes the full-width [128,1024] input-scale pass.
notes: AC-3/AC-3.1: commute (x@w)*inv_rms verified on HW (full 5-seed PASS); tensor_scalar reads PSUM accumulator directly (fused eviction). Latency 0.4733 vs same-session v1 0.4715 = +0.38% (within ~1.8% noise) -> valid ENABLER, not a promotion. PE_active_ms=0.97*0.4733=0.4591 (~unchanged vs v1 within profiler rounding). Vec 15->7% Scl 11->16% (input-scale pass removed).

The direct fp32 transposed HBM load route (Codex-flagged last off-PE check). nki.language.load_transpose2d (experimental) loads x's [m_in,128] K-sub-tile from HBM already transposed to [k_in,m_in], removing the transpose from PE AND Vector AND the dma_transpose path. AVAILABLE + CORRECT (full 5-seed PASS, 0.4706 ms). PE stays 97%, HBMrd/DMA unchanged. PE_active_ms=0.97*0.4706=0.4565 vs v1 0.4574 -> effectively unchanged within profiler rounding (PE% whole-percent). Latency -0.19% vs v1 (within noise, << 2.5% gate). NOT promoted (within-noise + experimental API). Decisive floor datum: even removing the PE transpose entirely yields no out-of-noise win -> transpose is fully hidden under the PE-bound matmul, never on the critical path.

Calibration (AC-2, record-only). bf16 main-matmul operands (transpose+PSUM+norm stay fp32). FAIL correctness 0/1 (bf16 mantissa ~4e-3 >> 2e-5 gate), as expected. fp32/bf16 ratio: D1 fp32 --fast 0.4706 / bf16 0.1458 = ~3.23x -> re-confirms hard fp32 PE penalty. fp32 is the structural ceiling; only lower precision beats it, which fails correctness. NOT promotable, never influences the fp32 path. (No PE% digest: profiler does not return summary_metrics for a correctness-failing run.)

Phase-3 fresh same-session v1 CONTROL. Full 5-seed PASS, 0.4714 ms (speedup 1.066x over baseline 0.502647). Anchors the noise band for all phase-3 candidate comparisons. 0.4714 vs historical 0.4716 (phase-1) / 0.4715 (phase-2 control) -> remote drift <0.05% (well inside the +-1.8% noise band). PE=97% MFU=46% (=bf16-peak floor 218.5us / 471.4us, the structural fp32 rate ceiling), Vec=15% Scl=11% DMA=19% HBMrd=25MB HBMwr=34MB. PE_active_ms=0.97*0.4714=0.4573 (coarse proxy; PE% whole-percent-rounded).

The main-matmul stationary-activation reuse reorder (the one main-matmul micro-lever phase 2 never touched). Reordered nc_matmul loop from N-chunk-outer/K-tile-inner to K-tile-outer/N-chunk-inner with 4 live [128,512] fp32 PSUM accumulators, so each stationary xT[kt] is presented once and streamed against all 4 N-chunks (256 stationary fills instead of 1024). Numerically equivalent to the v2_postscale base (same fp32 PSUM K-accumulation per output element; only the N loop moved inside the K loop) -> full 5-seed PASS (AC-3.1). --fast triage 0.4721 ms PASS 1/1; FULL 5-seed 0.4723 ms. +0.19% vs same-session v1 control 0.4714 = WITHIN the +-1.8% noise band, far under the 2.5% grey-zone gate -> NOT promoted (AC-3.2 expected-negative). PE stays pinned at 97%, MFU 46% unchanged; PE_active_ms=0.97*0.4723=0.4581 vs control 0.4573 (unchanged within whole-percent PE rounding). Vec 15->7%/Scl 11->17% shift is inherited from the post-scale eviction fold, not from the reorder. DECISIVE closing datum: reducing stationary fills 4x moved nothing measurable off the PE -> the stationary fills were already fully hidden under the PE-bound matmul, consistent with the phase-2 load_transpose2d result. Confirms no exposed main-matmul fill lever.

Offline numpy bf16x2 split pre-check (zero remote spend). Reproduces the EXACT scored input (np.random.seed(42), draw x then w, per adapter/nkibench_case.py DEFAULT_INPUT_SEED=42) and the NKIBench numpy reference (RMSNorm divide-by-K-inside-rms then normalize then matmul). bf16 round-to-nearest-even limb construction (x_hi=bf16(x), x_lo=bf16(x-x_hi)), 3-product sum x_hi*w_hi+x_hi*w_lo+x_lo*w_hi (drops x_lo*w_lo) accumulated in fp32 (models fp32 PSUM). VALIDATION (AC-4.1): fp32 post-scale control reproduces the reference to 4.84e-07 (~1e-7 role, confirms seed/draw-order/dtype/formula all match); plain bf16 = 2.35e-3 (~4e-3 P4 scale check). RESULT: worst bf16x2 3-product rel-L2 = 4.455e-06 across seeds {42,0,21,63,84,123,2024}, both post-scale and pre-scale variants ~identical. This is ~4.5x under the 2e-5 gate and ~3.4x under the 1.5e-5 DEC-2 comfortable-margin threshold -- MUCH better than the plan's naive ~1.5e-5 estimate, because the relative-L2 over the K=1024 dot-product accumulation partially cancels the per-operand-limb rounding error (the naive per-element ~2^-16 bound does not account for the sqrt(K)-style error averaging). 4-product (keeps lo*lo) = 3.49e-6 -> the dropped x_lo*w_lo term contributes only ~1e-6, negligible. DECISION (AC-4.2): offline worst 4.455e-06 <= 1.5e-5 -> COMFORTABLY BELOW -> AUTHORIZES one remote P3 full-5-seed attempt (still requires remote 5/5 PASS + out-of-noise latency win to promote, per AC-5).

Compensated bf16x2 split-matmul. Offline-gated: only attempted because the offline sim's worst idealized rel-L2 (4.455e-6) was comfortably <= the 1.5e-5 DEC-2 threshold (AC-4.2 authorized). Build: split each fp32 operand into two bf16 limbs (x_hi=bf16(x), x_lo=bf16(x-x_hi) RNE; w_hi/w_lo same, w split once resident), accumulate 3 bf16 products x_hi@w_hi + x_hi@w_lo + x_lo@w_hi in fp32 PSUM (drop negligible x_lo@w_lo ~1e-6), RMSNorm stays fp32 and per-row inv_rms applied post-scale at eviction (built on v2_postscale base to match the offline sim exactly; transpose is exact fp32 so splitting after transpose == before). MEASURED: --fast PASS 1/1 0.3687; FULL 5-seed PASS 0.3687 then confirmatory 0.3688 (byte-stable); same-session v1 control re-confirmed 0.4716. -21.8% vs control = 1.279x faster than v1; speedup over baseline 0.502647 jumps 1.066x -> 1.363x. FAR out of noise (>>2.5% band). MFU 46->45% PE 97->96% (bf16-rate matmul; PE now near-fully productive at the higher bf16 throughput), Vec 15->16% Scl 11->25% (limb-split casts+subtracts on Scalar/Vector, still hidden), DMA 19->23%, HBM unchanged (bf16 limbs built on-chip from the same fp32 loads). Clears BOTH AC-5 HARD gates: full-5-seed PASS AND out-of-noise latency win -> the ONLY path above the fp32 floor. PROMOTED (new best; supersedes v1's 1.066x). Correctness margin: offline idealized worst 4.455e-6, ~4.5x under the 2e-5 gate; hardware full-5-seed l2_norm_passed on all seeds confirms it holds on-device.

P2 contingency (fold the RMSNorm scale onto w-load instead of per-tile eviction) was to run ONLY if the P1 stationary-reuse reorder surfaced an unexpected exposed Vector/Scalar bubble. It did not: P1 profiled Vec=7% Scl=17% with PE pinned at 97% (both Vec and Scl comfortably hidden under the PE-bound matmul; no norm bubble appeared). The norm is measured-hidden and v2_postscale already moved the scale to eviction. P2 skipped by measurement, per the plan's default. (The subsequent bf16x2 split kernel keeps the same fp32 RMSNorm + post-scale eviction and shows Scl=25% still hidden under the now-bf16-rate matmul, further confirming no norm-fold is needed.)

Adversarial Codex review of the bf16x2 split promotion (analyze task). Verdict: PROMOTE bf16x2 split as the new best kernel; keep v1 as the pure-fp32 fallback. Confirms: (1) latency win credible & far out-of-noise (0.4716/0.3688=1.279x, 21.8% reduction, two byte-stable full runs 0.3687/0.3688 bracketed by re-confirmed control, vs ~1.8% noise). (2) Correctness clears the gate; honest caveat -- adapter fixes seed 42 for every profiler draw (adapter/nkibench_case.py:47) so on-device '5-seed' is weak on INPUT diversity, but the offline sim independently exercised 7 genuinely-distinct input draws {42,0,21,63,84,123,2024} all ~4.455e-6 (~4.5x under gate), so the correctness margin is robust across real input variation. (3) Dropped x_lo*w_lo is small (4-product only improves to 3.489e-6 -> omitted term not carrying the decision near the boundary). Small-norm-row risk not separately ruled out by relative-L2 but unlikely for this fixed RMSNorm+large-N,K-random-matmul distribution. (4) No hardware metric makes the win look fake: HBM unchanged expected (limbs built on-chip), Scl 11->25% is limb-construction cost not erasing the bf16 PE-rate gain. Residual risk (recorded, not blocking): if the true evaluator used genuinely distinct per-seed inputs, on-device 5-seed evidence would be overstated -- the offline margin makes that acceptable, not zero-risk.
